sections.title: Design Overview
sections.content:
## 2. Design Overview

### Solution Summary
The Guardrail Damage Detection System is implemented as a serverless, event-driven computer vision pipeline hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), utilizing an enterprise-aligned TypeScript/Node.js stack. The architecture decouples ingestion, processing, computer vision inference, human review, and geospatial reporting through managed AWS primitives. Videos are ingested securely via direct-to-S3 presigned multipart uploads initialized through a React frontend authenticated against county Active Directory via Amazon Cognito and AD FS. An event-driven architecture powered by Amazon EventBridge and AWS Step Functions orchestrates GPMF telemetry extraction, media segmentation via AWS Elemental MediaConvert, and distributed frame sampling via AWS Fargate containers.

Extracted frames are quality-filtered using an FFmpeg blurdetect filter before being passed through a TypeScript adapter layer to Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels object detection. The Step Functions workflow explicitly manages the inference endpoint lifecycle to control operational expenditure. Raw bounding-box detections are clustered by GPS proximity, time, and category into deduplicated review items stored in Amazon DynamoDB. County reviewers interact with a purpose-built React review application featuring bounding-box overlays and immutable audit logging. Confirmed damage findings are surfaced via an integrated Esri ArcGIS map dashboard and multi-format reporting engines utilizing shared query logic.

### Design Methodology
Domain-Driven Design (DDD) combined with Clean Architecture principles — separating core business logic (telemetry extraction, frame clustering, review state management) from external infrastructure concerns (AWS services, Esri ArcGIS APIs, React UI components) through explicit TypeScript interfaces, repository patterns, and service adapters.

### Key Design Principles
| Principle | How Applied |
|-----------|-------------|
| Separation of Concerns | Decouples video ingestion, telemetry extraction, AI inference, review workflows, and GIS reporting into dedicated microservices and serverless components. |
| Single Responsibility Principle | Each AWS Fargate task, Lambda function, and application module encapsulates a single discrete operation (e.g., FFmpeg blur filtering, GPMF parsing, detection clustering). |
| DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) | Utilizes shared TypeScript utility libraries for common data formatting, configuration management, and validation logic across frontend, backend, and processing services. |
| KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid) | Leverages managed cloud primitives (Amazon S3, DynamoDB, EventBridge, Step Functions, Rekognition Custom Labels) rather than custom-built infrastructure, minimizing operational overhead. |
| Fail-Safe & Resilience | Implements dead-letter queues (DLQs) for unhandled processing failures, point-in-time recovery on DynamoDB, and versioning on S3 to prevent silent pipeline drops and ensure data integrity. |

sections.title: UI/UX Design
sections.content:
## 3. UI/UX Design

### Screen Inventory
| Screen | Purpose | Route/Path | Auth Required |
|--------|---------|-----------|---------------|
| Login Screen | Authenticates county users via Amazon Cognito federated to Active Directory (AD FS) | `/login` | No |
| Video Upload Dashboard | Allows authorized users to upload long-form GoPro video files via presigned multipart uploads and track ingestion status | `/upload` | Yes — County Inspector / Administrator |
| Defect Review Queue & Workspace | Enables reviewers to inspect flagged guardrail defects with bounding-box overlays, review cluster metrics, and approve, dismiss, or recategorize items | `/review` | Yes — County Inspector / Reviewer |
| Map & Reporting Dashboard | Displays confirmed findings on an Esri ArcGIS map dashboard and provides multi-format export tools (CSV, PDF, GeoJSON) | `/reports` | Yes — County Inspector / Reviewer |

### User Flows
#### Flow 1: Video Ingestion and Upload
1. User navigates to `/login` and authenticates using county credentials via AD FS federation.
2. System validates the token and redirects the user to the `/upload` Video Upload Dashboard.
3. User selects a local long-form GoPro video file containing embedded GPMF telemetry and clicks "Upload".
4. System requests a presigned multipart upload URL from `/upload/presign`, splits the binary, and streams data directly to the S3 Raw Zone.
5. System displays upload completion status, and EventBridge triggers the automated Step Functions processing pipeline.

#### Flow 2: Human-in-the-Loop Defect Review and Audit Logging
1. Reviewer navigates to the `/review` Defect Review Queue after processing completes.
2. System retrieves paginated consolidated defect items from DynamoDB via `/defects`.
3. User selects a flagged defect item to open the workspace showing visual bounding-box overlays, category labels, confidence scores, and associated map location.
4. User reviews the item and performs an action: approves, dismisses (with a note), or recategorizes the defect.
5. System calls `/defects/{id}` via PATCH to update the review state, instantly persisting reviewer identity, timestamp, action, priority, and original versus corrected labels to the DynamoDB immutable audit log.

### Wireframe Descriptions
#### Login Screen
- **Layout:** Centered card layout on a neutral background featuring the county program title and a prominent single sign-on action.
- **Key Elements:** County branding header, "Sign in with County AD FS" button (triggering Amazon Cognito OAuth 2.0 flow).
- **States:** Loading (spinner during federation redirect), Error (invalid credentials or token expiration message).

#### Video Upload Dashboard
- **Layout:** Standard top navigation bar with user profile/logout, left-hand sidebar for navigation (`/upload`, `/review`, `/reports`), and a spacious main content drop zone.
- **Key Elements:** Drag-and-drop file upload zone, file selection button, active upload progress bar with percentage and chunk status, and a recent uploads status table.
- **States:** Empty (prompting file selection), Uploading (active progress bar), Success (confirmation badge and link to review queue), Error (multipart upload failure with retry option).

#### Defect Review Queue & Workspace
- **Layout:** Split-pane interface. Left pane contains a filterable, paginated data table/list of consolidated defect items; right pane displays the active item's detail view, geotagged still frame with visual bounding-box overlays, and decision controls.
- **Key Elements:** Category filter dropdowns (broken/severed, bent/deformed, missing, corroded/rusted, misaligned/leaning), priority assignment selectors (Critical, Urgent, Moderate), bounding-box canvas viewer, "Approve", "Dismiss", and "Recategorize" action buttons, and reason-code input text fields.
- **States:** Loading (skeleton loader for review queue), Empty ("No pending defects in queue"), Populated (active list and image preview), Error (failed API fetch from `/defects`).

#### Map & Reporting Dashboard
- **Layout:** Full-screen Esri ArcGIS map embedded in the main content area with a collapsible reporting and export control panel on the right side.
- **Key Elements:** Interactive Esri ArcGIS map view with clustered map pins grouped by defect category, date range picker, road segment filter, and export buttons for CSV, printable/PDF inspection reports, and GeoJSON.
- **States:** Loading (map tile spinner), Populated (rendered map layers and interactive markers), Empty ("No confirmed findings match current filters"), Error (GIS service connection failure).

### Responsive Design
- **Breakpoints:** Mobile (320px - 768px), Tablet (769px - 1024px), Desktop (1025px and above).
- **Approach:** Desktop-first for the primary review workstation and map dashboard (optimized for high-resolution inspector monitors), with responsive container collapsing for mobile and tablet views during field uploads or read-only status checks.

### Accessibility
- **WCAG Level:** WCAG 2.1 AA
- **Key Considerations:** Full keyboard navigation support for data tables and review action buttons; screen-reader compatible ARIA labels for bounding-box metadata and review status badges; high contrast color palettes for defect category indicators; explicit focus management during modal interactions in the review workflow.

sections.title: API Design
sections.content:
## 4. API Design

### API Style
REST — Selected because the architecture relies on standard HTTP-based CRUD and patch operations for frontend application communication (React Upload and Reviewer apps) and downstream Esri ArcGIS integrations, utilizing Amazon API Gateway for routing.

### API Versioning
URL path versioning (`/v1/`) — Selected to ensure explicit client contract stability and backwards compatibility as the React applications and external integrations evolve.

### Endpoint Catalog

#### Upload Management

##### POST /v1/upload/presign
- **Purpose:** Generates an Amazon S3 presigned multipart upload URL to allow direct-to-S3 ingestion of long-form GoPro video files, bypassing API Gateway payload size limits.
- **Auth:** Authorized county user (`County Inspector / Reviewer` or `County Administrator / Uploader`) via Amazon Cognito JWT Bearer Token (AD FS federation).
- **Rate Limit:** 30 requests/minute
- **Request Body:**
```json
{
  "fileName": "string (required) — original filename of the GoPro inspection video",
  "fileSize": "number (required) — size of the video file in bytes",
  "contentType": "string (required) — MIME type of the video file (e.g., video/mp4)"
}
```
- **Response (200):**
```json
{
  "uploadId": "string — unique multipart upload identifier assigned by S3",
  "s3Key": "string — target object key in the S3 Raw Zone bucket",
  "presignedUrl": "string — secure presigned URL for uploading video parts",
  "expiresAt": "ISO 8601 datetime — expiration timestamp for the presigned URL"
}
```
- **Error Responses:** 400 (validation), 401 (unauthorized), 403 (forbidden), 500 (internal server error)
- **Requirement Trace:** FR-001

---

#### Defect Review & Management

##### GET /v1/defects
- **Purpose:** Retrieves paginated and filtered lists of consolidated defect items for display in the React reviewer application.
- **Auth:** Authorized county reviewer via Amazon Cognito JWT Bearer Token (AD FS federation).
- **Rate Limit:** 100 requests/minute
- **Request Body:** None (Query parameters used for filtering: `status`, `category`, `priority`, `limit`, `nextToken`)
- **Response (200):**
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "defectId": "string — unique consolidated defect item ID",
      "category": "string — defect category (broken-severed, bent-deformed, missing, corroded-rusted, misaligned-leaning)",
      "status": "string — current review status (pending, approved, dismissed, recategorized)",
      "priority": "string — assigned priority (Critical, Urgent, Moderate)",
      "confidence": "number — AI model confidence score (0.0 to 1.0)",
      "boundingBox": {
        "ymin": "number — normalized top coordinate",
        "xmin": "number — normalized left coordinate",
        "ymax": "number — normalized bottom coordinate",
        "xmax": "number — normalized right coordinate"
      },
      "gpsCoordinates": {
        "latitude": "number — latitude coordinate",
        "longitude": "number — longitude coordinate"
      },
      "timestamp": "ISO 8601 datetime — capture timestamp",
      "frameImageUrl": "string — presigned S3 URL of the representative frame image"
    }
  ],
  "nextToken": "string (optional) — pagination token for fetching subsequent records"
}
```
- **Error Responses:** 400 (validation), 401 (unauthorized), 403 (forbidden), 500 (internal server error)
- **Requirement Trace:** FR-007

---

##### PATCH /v1/defects/{id}
- **Purpose:** Updates a consolidated defect item's review status (approve, dismiss, recategorize) and records an immutable audit log entry in Amazon DynamoDB.
- **Auth:** Authorized county reviewer via Amazon Cognito JWT Bearer Token (AD FS federation).
- **Rate Limit:** 60 requests/minute
- **Request Body:**
```json
{
  "action": "string (required) — review action taken (APPROVE, DISMISS, RECATEGORIZE)",
  "priority": "string (optional) — assigned priority (Critical, Urgent, Moderate)",
  "correctedCategory": "string (optional) — new category label if recategorized",
  "dismissalNote": "string (optional) — required note explaining dismissal reason if action is DISMISS"
}
```
- **Response (200):**
```json
{
  "defectId": "string — updated defect item ID",
  "status": "string — updated review status",
  "priority": "string — updated priority",
  "auditRecord": {
    "reviewerId": "string — user ID from JWT claims",
    "timestamp": "ISO 8601 datetime — exact time of review decision",
    "originalAiLabel": "string — original label assigned by AI model",
    "correctedLabel": "string (optional) — corrected label if modified",
    "action": "string — action performed"
  }
}
```
- **Error Responses:** 400 (validation), 401 (unauthorized), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 500 (internal server error)
- **Requirement Trace:** FR-007

---

#### Reporting & GIS Integration

##### GET /v1/reports
- **Purpose:** Exports inspection reports and summaries in CSV, PDF, or GeoJSON formats derived from DynamoDB and shared query logic.
- **Auth:** Authorized county user/reviewer via Amazon Cognito JWT Bearer Token (AD FS federation).
- **Rate Limit:** 20 requests/minute
- **Request Body:** None (Query parameters: `format` [csv, pdf, geojson], `startDate`, `endDate`, `priority`)
- **Response (200):**
```json
{
  "reportId": "string — unique report generation ID",
  "format": "string — requested export format",
  "downloadUrl": "string — presigned S3 URL to download the generated report file",
  "generatedAt": "ISO 8601 datetime — generation timestamp"
}
```
- **Error Responses:** 400 (validation), 401 (unauthorized), 403 (forbidden), 500 (internal server error)
- **Requirement Trace:** FR-008

---

##### GET /v1/gis/query
- **Purpose:** Provides spatial and attribute data via shared query logic to support the county's Esri ArcGIS map dashboard and geospatial layer rendering.
- **Auth:** Authorized county GIS stakeholder via Amazon Cognito JWT Bearer Token (AD FS federation).
- **Rate Limit:** 100 requests/minute
- **Request Body:** None (Query parameters: `bbox` [bounding box coordinates], `category`, `status`)
- **Response (200):**
```json
{
  "type": "FeatureCollection",
  "features": [
    {
      "type": "Feature",
      "geometry": {
        "type": "Point",
        "coordinates": [
          "number — longitude",
          "number — latitude"
        ]
      },
      "properties": {
        "defectId": "string — unique defect ID",
        "category": "string — defect category",
        "priority": "string — priority level",
        "status": "string — review status",
        "reviewedBy": "string — reviewer ID",
        "timestamp": "ISO 8601 datetime"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
- **Error Responses:** 400 (validation), 401 (unauthorized), 403 (forbidden), 500 (internal server error)
- **Requirement Trace:** FR-008

---

### Standard Error Response Format
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "ERROR_CODE",
    "message": "Human-readable message describing the error",
    "details": [
      {
        "field": "string — invalid or missing field name",
        "issue": "string — description of the validation failure"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```json
        "timestamp": "ISO 8601 datetime"
      }
    }
  ]

```
- **Error Responses:** 400 (validation), 401 (unauthorized), 403 (forbidden), 500 (internal server error)
- **Requirement Trace:** FR-008

---

### Standard Error Response Format
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "ERROR_CODE",
    "message": "Human-readable message describing the error",
    "details": [
      {
        "field": "string — invalid or missing field name",
```

| updatedAt | Number (Timestamp) | NOT NULL | Epoch timestamp when the video session was last updated |

**Indexes:**
| Index Name | Fields | Type | Justification |
|-----------|--------|------|---------------|
| `StatusIndex` | `processingStatus` (HASH), `createdAt` (RANGE) | Global Secondary Index (GSI) | Enables efficient querying and monitoring of jobs by their current pipeline status and creation time for operational dashboards and debugging. |
| `UserSessionsIndex` | `uploaderUserId` (HASH), `createdAt` (RANGE) | Global Secondary Index (GSI) | Allows county users and administrators to view their historical video upload and processing sessions sorted by date. |

---

#### Entity 2: Frames
| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|-------|------|------------|-------------|
| frameId | String (PK format: `{sessionId}#{frameNumber}`) | PK, NOT NULL | Composite primary key combining session ID and sequence number |
| sessionId | String | NOT NULL, SK | Partition key reference to the parent video processing session |
| frameNumber | Number | NOT NULL, SK | Sequential frame index within the video session |
| s3FrameKey | String | NOT NULL | S3 storage key for the extracted, quality-filtered still frame |
| timestamp | Number | NOT NULL | Video timestamp in milliseconds |
| latitude | Number | NOT NULL | GPS latitude coordinate attached during extraction |
| longitude | Number | NOT NULL | GPS longitude coordinate attached during extraction |
| blurScore | Number | NOT NULL | Numeric score returned by the FFmpeg blurdetect filter |
| isUsable | Boolean | NOT NULL | Flag indicating whether the frame passed the quality gate |

**Indexes:**
| Index Name | Fields | Type | Justification |
|-----------|--------|------|---------------|
| `SessionFramesIndex` | `sessionId` (HASH), `timestamp` (RANGE) | Global Secondary Index (GSI) | Enables efficient retrieval and chronological traversal of frames associated with a specific inspection session. |

---

#### Entity 3: ConsolidatedDefects
| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|-------|------|------------|-------------|
| defectId | String (UUID) | PK, NOT NULL | Unique identifier for the consolidated, deduplicated review item |
| sessionId | String | NOT NULL | Parent video processing session ID |
| category | String | NOT NULL | Defect category (broken_severed, bent_deformed, missing, corroded_rusted, misaligned_leaning_posts) |
| latitude | Number | NOT NULL | Representative GPS latitude coordinate of the clustered physical defect |
| longitude | Number | NOT NULL | Representative GPS longitude coordinate of the clustered physical defect |
| boundingBox | Map | NOT NULL | Bounding box coordinates (`ymin`, `xmin`, `ymax`, `xmax`) from the representative frame |
| confidenceScore | Number | NOT NULL | AI model confidence score associated with the detection |
| reviewStatus | String | NOT NULL | Current review state (PENDING, APPROVED, DISMISSED, RECATEGORIZED) |
| priority | String | NULLABLE | Assigned severity priority (CRITICAL, URGENT, MODERATE) |
| createdAt | Number (Timestamp) | NOT NULL | Epoch timestamp when the defect was consolidated and added to the review queue |

**Indexes:**
| Index Name | Fields | Type | Justification |
|-----------|--------|------|---------------|
| `ReviewStatusIndex` | `reviewStatus` (HASH), `createdAt` (RANGE) | Global Secondary Index (GSI) | Powers the React reviewer application queue by allowing inspectors to query pending or reviewed defect items sorted by creation time. |
| `SessionDefectsIndex` | `sessionId` (HASH), `category` (RANGE) | Global Secondary Index (GSI) | Facilitates querying and reporting of defects grouped by video session and category for inspection summaries. |
| `SpatialGeoIndex` | `category` (HASH), `latitude` (RANGE) | Global Secondary Index (GSI) | Enables geospatial and categorical filtering to support Esri ArcGIS map dashboard queries and spatial data retrieval. |

---

#### Entity 4: ReviewAuditTrail
| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|-------|------|------------|-------------|
| auditId | String (UUID) | PK, NOT NULL | Unique primary key for the immutable audit log entry |
| defectId | String | NOT NULL | Reference to the consolidated defect item being reviewed |
| reviewerUserId | String | NOT NULL | Cognito user ID of the county reviewer making the decision |
| action | String | NOT NULL | Review action taken (APPROVE, DISMISS, RECATEGORIZE) |
| originalAiLabel | String | NOT NULL | The original defect category assigned by Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels |
| correctedLabel | String | NULLABLE | The corrected defect category if recategorized by the reviewer |
| dismissalReason | String | NULLABLE | Optional notes or justification provided when dismissing a defect |
| timestamp | Number (Timestamp) | NOT NULL | Epoch timestamp when the review decision was recorded |

**Indexes:**
| Index Name | Fields | Type | Justification |
|-----------|--------|------|---------------|
| `DefectAuditIndex` | `defectId` (HASH), `timestamp` (RANGE) | Global Secondary Index (GSI) | Allows rapid retrieval of the complete audit history and decision timeline for any specific defect item. |
| `ReviewerActivityIndex` | `reviewerUserId` (HASH), `timestamp` (RANGE) | Global Secondary Index (GSI) | Enables tracking of reviewer productivity, activity logs, and auditing compliance metrics over time. |

---

### Migration Strategy
- **Tool:** AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) with TypeScript (`aws-cdk-lib/aws-dynamodb`), paired with application-level schema versioning in code.
- **Approach:** Forward-only schema evolution. Since Amazon DynamoDB is a schemaless NoSQL database, table structures and Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs) are provisioned declaratively via Infrastructure as Code (CDK). Application code handles optional/new attributes gracefully using defensive property checks and default values.
- **Naming:** Timestamp-based stack deployment versions combined with explicit DynamoDB table name prefixing (`cc-{env}-VideoProcessingSessions`, `cc-{env}-Frames`, `cc-{env}-ConsolidatedDefects`, `cc-{env}-ReviewAuditTrail`).

### Seed Data
| Entity | Records Needed | Purpose |
|--------|---------------|---------|
| ConsolidatedDefects | 5 (1 per defect category) | Demonstration and UI validation within the React Reviewer application and Esri ArcGIS map dashboard during local development and integration testing. |
| VideoProcessingSessions | 2 | End-to-end pipeline verification, testing upload session state transitions, and validating user session retrieval queries. |

sections.content:
## 6. Component/Module Design

### React Upload Application

**Responsibility:** Provide a secure user interface for authenticated county users to upload long-form GoPro video files containing embedded GPMF telemetry directly to S3 via presigned multipart uploads.
**Technology:** React (TypeScript) hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed via Amazon CloudFront, integrated with Amazon Cognito.

**Public Interface:**
```
renderUploadPage(): JSX.Element — Renders the authenticated file upload dashboard view
handleAuthentication(): Promise<void> — Manages user login state via Amazon Cognito and AD FS federation
requestPresignedUrl(fileName: string, fileSize: number): Promise<PresignedUploadResponse> — Calls backend API to generate S3 presigned multipart upload URLs
uploadVideoFile(file: File, onProgress: (progress: number) => void): Promise<string> — Executes client-side multipart chunk upload directly to Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon Cognito: User authentication and AD FS session management
- Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket: Target destination for direct presigned multipart video uploads via HTTPS

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. User authenticates via React frontend using Amazon Cognito federated to county AD FS.
2. User selects a local GoPro video file in the upload interface.
3. Frontend requests presigned multipart upload parts from the backend API (`/upload/presign`).
4. Frontend chunks the video file and uploads parts directly to the Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket via HTTPS.
5. Upon successful completion of all parts, frontend finalizes the multipart upload with S3 and displays confirmation.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `REACT_APP_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID` | string | `us-east-1_example` | Amazon Cognito User Pool identifier |
| `REACT_APP_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID` | string | `example_client_id` | Amazon Cognito App Client ID |
| `REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL` | string | `https://api.example.com` | Base URL for backend API endpoints |
| `REACT_APP_S3_RAW_BUCKET` | string | `county-guardrail-raw-video-bucket` | Target S3 bucket name for raw uploads |

---

### React Reviewer Application

**Responsibility:** Provide a web interface for reviewing flagged guardrail defects with bounding-box overlays, managing review queues, recording inspection decisions (approve, dismiss, recategorize), and displaying reporting data.
**Technology:** React (TypeScript) hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed via Amazon CloudFront, querying Amazon DynamoDB via API endpoints.

**Public Interface:**
```
renderReviewQueue(): JSX.Element — Renders paginated and filtered list of consolidated defect review items
renderDefectDetailModal(defectId: string): JSX.Element — Renders interactive modal with bounding-box image overlay and audit details
updateDefectStatus(defectId: string, action: 'approve' | 'dismiss' | 'recategorize', payload: ReviewPayload): Promise<void> — Submits reviewer decision to update DynamoDB record and audit trail
exportInspectionReports(format: 'csv' | 'pdf' | 'geojson'): Promise<Blob> — Requests formatted inspection data exports from backend API
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon Cognito: Authenticating reviewing users via JWT bearer tokens
- Amazon DynamoDB: Retrieving consolidated defect items and persisting immutable audit trail entries

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Reviewer authenticates via Amazon Cognito and loads the React Reviewer Application.
2. Application fetches paginated consolidated defect items from backend API (`/defects`).
3. Reviewer selects a defect item to inspect image frames with bounding-box overlays.
4. Reviewer submits a decision (approve, dismiss with note, or recategorize with new label and priority assignment).
5. Frontend transmits the patch request (`/defects/{id}`), persisting the reviewer ID, timestamp, original AI label, and corrected label to Amazon DynamoDB.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `REACT_APP_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID` | string | `us-east-1_example` | Amazon Cognito User Pool identifier |
| `REACT_APP_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID` | string | `example_client_id` | Amazon Cognito App Client ID |
| `REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL` | string | `https://api.example.com` | Base URL for backend API endpoints |

---

### AWS Step Functions Pipeline

**Responsibility:** Orchestrate the multi-stage video processing workflow, handle explicit start/stop commands for the Rekognition inference endpoint, manage distributed map parallelization, and route execution errors.
**Technology:** AWS Step Functions (Standard Workflow with Distributed Map).

**Public Interface:**
```
startWorkflow(executionInput: WorkflowInput): Promise<string> — Initiates Step Functions execution returning execution ARN
getWorkflowStatus(executionArn: string): Promise<WorkflowStatusResponse> — Queries execution status and stage telemetry
handleExecutionError(errorPayload: ErrorPayload): Promise<void> — Routes unhandled processing failures to Dead-Letter Queue (SQS)
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon EventBridge: Receives S3 object-created events to trigger workflow initiation
- AWS Elemental MediaConvert: Executes video segmentation jobs
- AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction & Frame Processing Services: Executes parallel container tasks
- Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels: Managed AI inference endpoint controlled via explicit start/stop states
- Amazon S3 & Amazon DynamoDB: Intermediary data storage and final persistence

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Triggered via EventBridge when a raw video lands in S3.
2. Step Functions invokes AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction task to generate normalized GPS track in S3.
3. Step Functions invokes AWS Elemental MediaConvert to segment video chunks.
4. Step Functions starts the Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels inference endpoint.
5. Step Functions uses a Distributed Map state to fan out parallel Fargate Frame Processing tasks (sampling every 3 meters, blur filtering, Rekognition inference, and clustering).
6. Step Functions stops the Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels inference endpoint upon completion or error.
7. Final consolidated records are written to Amazon DynamoDB.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `STEP_FUNCTIONS_STATE_MACHINE_ARN` | string | `arn:aws:states:us-east-1:123456789012:stateMachine:GuardrailPipeline` | Target state machine ARN |
| `REKOGNITION_PROJECT_VERSION_ARN` | string | `arn:aws:rekognition:us-east-1:123456789012:project/Guardrail/version/v1` | Target Custom Labels model version ARN |
| `DLQ_QUEUE_URL` | string | `https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/processing-dlq` | Dead-Letter Queue URL for pipeline failures |

---

### AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction Service

**Responsibility:** Decode the complete GPMF telemetry stream from original, unmodified video files prior to transcoding and write a normalized GPS track (JSON/Parquet) to S3.
**Technology:** Node.js / TypeScript running inside an AWS Fargate container task with binary stream parsing libraries.

**Public Interface:**
```
extractGpmfStream(s3Bucket: string, s3Key: string): Promise<GpmfStreamResult> — Downloads raw video stream and parses embedded GPMF metadata tracks
generateNormalizedGpsTrack(rawTelemetry: GpmfMetadata[]): GpsTrackItem[] — Converts raw telemetry into timestamp-indexed GPS track array
persistGpsTrackToS3(destinationBucket: string, destinationKey: string, trackData: GpsTrackItem[]): Promise<void> — Writes normalized GPS JSON/Parquet track to S3 Processed Bucket
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket: Source for uncompressed GoPro video files
- Amazon S3 Processed Data Bucket: Target destination for normalized GPS tracks (JSON/Parquet)

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Container task receives S3 bucket and object key from Step Functions workflow.
2. Task downloads byte ranges or streams the unmodified GoPro video file from S3.
3. Task parses the GPMF metadata container to extract precise GPS coordinates, timestamps, and validity flags.
4. Task normalizes telemetry into a timestamp-indexed GPS track structure.
5. Task writes the normalized GPS track file to the S3 Processed Data Bucket.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `PROCESSED_DATA_BUCKET` | string | `county-guardrail-processed-data-bucket` | S3 bucket destination for GPS tracks |
| `FARGATE_TASK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | number | 1800 | Maximum container execution timeout |

---

### AWS Fargate Frame Processing Service

**Responsibility:** Execute distributed map tasks to sample video frames at distance intervals (every 3 meters), apply FFmpeg blur detection filtering, and correlate frames against normalized GPS tracks.
**Technology:** Node.js / TypeScript running inside an AWS Fargate container task with bundled FFmpeg binaries and image processing utilities.

**Public Interface:**
```
downloadVideoChunk(chunkBucket: string, chunkKey: string): Promise<string> — Downloads video segment chunk locally inside container
sampleFramesByDistance(videoPath: string, gpsTrack: GpsTrackItem[], intervalMeters: number): Promise<ExtractedFrame[]> — Samples video frames every 3 meters using GPS track correlation
applyBlurFilter(framePath: string): Promise<boolean> — Evaluates frame using FFmpeg blurdetect filter; returns true if acceptable quality
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon S3 Processed Data Bucket: Source for normalized GPS tracks and target for extracted frames
- AWS Elemental MediaConvert: Source for transcoded video chunk files in S3

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Task receives chunk metadata, GPS track location, and sampling parameters from Step Functions Distributed Map.
2. Task downloads the assigned video chunk from S3.
3. Task calculates precise frame extraction timestamps corresponding to 3-meter distance intervals using the normalized GPS track.
4. Task extracts image frames at calculated timestamps.
5. Task passes each extracted frame through an FFmpeg blurdetect filter, dropping blurry or unreliable frames.
6. Surviving high-quality geotagged frames and sidecar JSON metadata are uploaded to the S3 Processed Data Bucket.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `SAMPLING_INTERVAL_METERS` | number | 3 | Target distance interval for frame sampling |
| `BLUR_THRESHOLD_CONFIG` | number | 0.5 | Minimum threshold score for FFmpeg blurdetect filter acceptance |
| `PROCESSED_DATA_BUCKET` | string | `county-guardrail-processed-data-bucket` | S3 destination for extracted frames |

---

### Detection Service Adapter Layer & Model Integration

**Responsibility:** Abstract and handle communication between processing tasks and the underlying computer vision model (Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels), submitting usable frames and receiving bounding boxes and categories.
**Technology:** TypeScript module embedded within Fargate container tasks utilizing `@aws-sdk/client-rekognition`.

**Public Interface:**
```
submitFrameForDetection(frameBuffer: Buffer, modelArn: string): Promise<DetectionResult[]> — Submits frame buffer to Rekognition Custom Labels and parses response
parseBoundingBoxes(rekognitionResponse: DetectCustomLabelsCommandOutput): DetectionResult[] — Extracts normalized bounding boxes, categories, and confidence scores
filterDetectionsByConfidence(detections: DetectionResult[], threshold: number): DetectionResult[] — Filters raw detections against configured confidence threshold
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels: Managed computer vision inference endpoint (`DetectCustomLS` / `DetectCustomLabels` API)

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Fargate frame processing task loads an extracted, quality-filtered still frame into memory.
2. Adapter layer wraps the image buffer and calls `DetectCustomLabels` against the active Rekognition model endpoint.
3. Adapter parses the JSON response, extracting bounding box coordinates, defect categories (broken/severed, bent/deformed, missing, corroded/rusted, misaligned/leaning posts), and confidence scores.
4. Adapter filters out detections falling below the versioned confidence threshold.
5. Filtered detection payloads are passed to the clustering and consolidation engine.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `REKOGNITION_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD` | number | 80.0 | Minimum confidence percentage score required for valid detection |
| `MAX_RESULTS_PER_IMAGE` | number | 10 | Maximum bounding box detections allowed per frame |

---

### Detection Consolidation & Clustering Service

**Responsibility:** Cluster raw bounding-box detections of the same physical defect across multiple nearby frames using GPS proximity, time, and category into a single representative review item stored in DynamoDB.
**Technology:** Node.js / TypeScript service execution module running within AWS Fargate / Lambda processing tasks.

**Public Interface:**
```
clusterRawDetections(rawDetections: FrameDetectionRecord[]): ConsolidatedDefectItem[] — Groups raw bounding-box hits by GPS proximity, time window, and category
calculateClusterCentroid(clusterDetections: FrameDetectionRecord[]): GpsCoordinates — Computes median GPS coordinates and representative best-confidence bounding box
persistConsolidatedDefects(consolidatedItems: ConsolidatedDefectItem[]): Promise<void> — Writes deduplicated review items and metadata to Amazon DynamoDB
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon DynamoDB: Target data store for consolidated review items and audit records

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Collects all raw bounding-box detections generated across sequential processed frames for an inspection run.
2. Applies spatial clustering (GPS proximity within tolerance radius) and temporal/category matching to identify repeated hits of the same physical defect.
3. Collapses clustered detections into a single representative review item, selecting the frame with the highest confidence score for visual inspection overlay.
4. Writes consolidated defect items, bounding-box metadata, and initial queue status to Amazon DynamoDB.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `GPS_PROXIMITY_CLUSTER_RADIUS_METERS` | number | 5.0 | Spatial radius threshold for clustering identical defects |
| `DYNAMODB_DEFECT_TABLE_NAME` | string | `GuardrailDefectsTable` | Target DynamoDB table name for consolidated review items |

---

### Esri ArcGIS Integration Service

**Responsibility:** Integrate confirmed damage findings and shared query logic with the county's existing Esri ArcGIS platform to support map dashboards, GIS layers, and export reporting.
**Technology:** Node.js / TypeScript integration service interfacing with Esri ArcGIS REST APIs and Amazon DynamoDB.

**Public Interface:**
```
queryConfirmedFindings(queryParams: GisQueryParameters): Promise<ArcGISFeatureCollection> — Queries confirmed DynamoDB damage records and formats as GeoJSON feature collection
publishToArcGISFeatureLayer(featureCollection: ArcGISFeatureCollection): Promise<ArcGISPublishResponse> — Publishes or updates confirmed defect features on county Esri ArcGIS layer
generateInspectionReport(reportFormat: 'csv' | 'pdf', filterCriteria: ReportFilterCriteria): Promise<Buffer> — Compiles road/priority summaries and generates exportable report documents
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon DynamoDB: Source database for confirmed damage findings and audit records
- Esri ArcGIS Platform: External county GIS mapping and feature service endpoints

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Service receives scheduled or user-initiated requests for map data or inspection reports.
2. Service queries Amazon DynamoDB using shared query logic to retrieve confirmed damage records filtered by category, road segment, or priority.

### React Upload Application

**Responsibility:** Provide a secure user interface for authenticated county users to upload long-form GoPro video files containing embedded GPMF telemetry directly to S3 via presigned multipart uploads.
**Technology:** React (TypeScript) hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed via Amazon CloudFront, integrated with Amazon Cognito.

**Public Interface:**
```
renderUploadPage(): JSX.Element — Renders the authenticated file upload dashboard view
handleAuthentication(): Promise<void> — Manages user login state via Amazon Cognito and AD FS federation
requestPresignedUrl(fileName: string, fileSize: number): Promise<PresignedUploadResponse> — Calls backend API to generate S3 presigned multipart upload URLs
uploadVideoFile(file: File, onProgress: (progress: number) => void): Promise<string> — Executes client-side multipart chunk upload directly to Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon Cognito: User authentication and AD FS session management
- Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket: Target destination for direct presigned multipart video uploads via HTTPS

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. User authenticates via React frontend using Amazon Cognito federated to county AD FS.
2. User selects a local GoPro video file in the upload interface.
3. Frontend requests presigned multipart upload parts from the backend API (`/upload/presign`).

---

### React Reviewer Application

**Responsibility:** Provide a web interface for reviewing flagged guardrail defects with bounding-box overlays, managing review queues, recording inspection decisions (approve, dismiss, recategorize), and displaying reporting data.
**Technology:** React (TypeScript) hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed via Amazon CloudFront, querying Amazon DynamoDB via API endpoints.

**Public Interface:**
```
renderReviewQueue(): JSX.Element — Renders paginated and filtered list of consolidated defect review items
renderDefectDetailModal(defectId: string): JSX.Element — Renders interactive modal with bounding-box image overlay and audit details
updateDefectStatus(defectId: string, action: 'approve' | 'dismiss' | 'recategorize', payload: ReviewPayload): Promise<void> — Submits reviewer decision to update DynamoDB record and audit trail
exportInspectionReports(format: 'csv' | 'pdf' | 'geojson'): Promise<Blob> — Requests formatted inspection data exports from backend API
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon Cognito: Authenticating reviewing users via JWT bearer tokens
- Amazon DynamoDB: Retrieving consolidated defect items and persisting immutable audit trail entries

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Reviewer authenticates via Amazon Cognito and loads the React Reviewer Application.
2. Application fetches paginated consolidated defect items from backend API (`/defects`).
3. Reviewer selects a defect item to inspect image frames with bounding-box overlays.
4. Reviewer submits a decision (approve, dismiss with note, or recategorize with new label and priority assignment).
5. Frontend transmits the patch request (`/defects/{id}`), persisting the reviewer ID, timestamp, original AI label, and corrected label to Amazon DynamoDB.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `REACT_APP_COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID` | string | `us-east-1_example` | Amazon Cognito User Pool identifier |
| `REACT_APP_COGNITO_CLIENT_ID` | string | `example_client_id` | Amazon Cognito App Client ID |
| `REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL` | string | `https://api.example.com` | Base URL for backend API endpoints |

---

### AWS Step Functions Pipeline

**Responsibility:** Orchestrate the multi-stage video processing workflow, handle explicit start/stop commands for the Rekognition inference endpoint, manage distributed map parallelization, and route execution errors.
**Technology:** AWS Step Functions (Standard Workflow with Distributed Map).

**Public Interface:**
```
startWorkflow(executionInput: WorkflowInput): Promise<string> — Initiates Step Functions execution returning execution ARN
getWorkflowStatus(executionArn: string): Promise<WorkflowStatusResponse> — Queries execution status and stage telemetry
handleExecutionError(errorPayload: ErrorPayload): Promise<void> — Routes unhandled processing failures to Dead-Letter Queue (SQS)
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon EventBridge: Receives S3 object-created events to trigger workflow initiation
- AWS Elemental MediaConvert: Executes video segmentation jobs
- AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction & Frame Processing Services: Executes parallel container tasks
- Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels: Managed AI inference endpoint controlled via explicit start/stop states
- Amazon S3 & Amazon DynamoDB: Intermediary data storage and final persistence

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Triggered via EventBridge when a raw video lands in S3.
2. Step Functions invokes AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction task to generate normalized GPS track in S3.
3. Step Functions invokes AWS Elemental MediaConvert to segment video chunks.
4. Step Functions starts the Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels inference endpoint.
5. Step Functions uses a Distributed Map state to fan out parallel Fargate Frame Processing tasks (sampling every 3 meters, blur filtering, Rekognition inference, and clustering).
6. Step Functions stops the Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels inference endpoint upon completion or error.
7. Final consolidated records are written to Amazon DynamoDB.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `STEP_FUNCTIONS_STATE_MACHINE_ARN` | string | `arn:aws:states:us-east-1:123456789012:stateMachine:GuardrailPipeline` | Target state machine ARN |
| `REKOGNITION_PROJECT_VERSION_ARN` | string | `arn:aws:rekognition:us-east-1:123456789012:project/Guardrail/version/v1` | Target Custom Labels model version ARN |
| `DLQ_QUEUE_URL` | string | `https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/processing-dlq` | Dead-Letter Queue URL for pipeline failures |

---

### AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction Service

**Responsibility:** Decode the complete GPMF telemetry stream from original, unmodified video files prior to transcoding and write a normalized GPS track (JSON/Parquet) to S3.
**Technology:** Node.js / TypeScript running inside an AWS Fargate container task with binary stream parsing libraries.

**Public Interface:**
```
extractGpmfStream(s3Bucket: string, s3Key: string): Promise<GpmfStreamResult> — Downloads raw video stream and parses embedded GPMF metadata tracks
generateNormalizedGpsTrack(rawTelemetry: GpmfMetadata[]): GpsTrackItem[] — Converts raw telemetry into timestamp-indexed GPS track array
persistGpsTrackToS3(destinationBucket: string, destinationKey: string, trackData: GpsTrackItem[]): Promise<void> — Writes normalized GPS JSON/Parquet track to S3 Processed Bucket
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket: Source for uncompressed GoPro video files
- Amazon S3 Processed Data Bucket: Target destination for normalized GPS tracks (JSON/Parquet)

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Container task receives S3 bucket and object key from Step Functions workflow.
2. Task downloads byte ranges or streams the unmodified GoPro video file from S3.
3. Task parses the GPMF metadata container to extract precise GPS coordinates, timestamps, and validity flags.
4. Task normalizes telemetry into a timestamp-indexed GPS track structure.
5. Task writes the normalized GPS track file to the S3 Processed Data Bucket.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `PROCESSED_DATA_BUCKET` | string | `county-guardrail-processed-data-bucket` | S3 bucket destination for GPS tracks |
| `FARGATE_TASK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | number | 1800 | Maximum container execution timeout |

---

### AWS Fargate Frame Processing Service

**Responsibility:** Execute distributed map tasks to sample video frames at distance intervals (every 3 meters), apply FFmpeg blur detection filtering, and correlate frames against normalized GPS tracks.
**Technology:** Node.js / TypeScript running inside an AWS Fargate container task with bundled FFmpeg binaries and image processing utilities.

**Public Interface:**
```
downloadVideoChunk(chunkBucket: string, chunkKey: string): Promise<string> — Downloads video segment chunk locally inside container
sampleFramesByDistance(videoPath: string, gpsTrack: GpsTrackItem[], intervalMeters: number): Promise<ExtractedFrame[]> — Samples video frames every 3 meters using GPS track correlation
applyBlurFilter(framePath: string): Promise<boolean> — Evaluates frame using FFmpeg blurdetect filter; returns true if acceptable quality
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon S3 Processed Data Bucket: Source for normalized GPS tracks and target for extracted frames
- AWS Elemental MediaConvert: Source for transcoded video chunk files in S3

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Task receives chunk metadata, GPS track location, and sampling parameters from Step Functions Distributed Map.
2. Task downloads the assigned video chunk from S3.
3. Task calculates precise frame extraction timestamps corresponding to 3-meter distance intervals using the normalized GPS track.
4. Task extracts image frames at calculated timestamps.
5. Task passes each extracted frame through an FFmpeg blurdetect filter, dropping blurry or unreliable frames.
6. Surviving high-quality geotagged frames and sidecar JSON metadata are uploaded to the S3 Processed Data Bucket.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `SAMPLING_INTERVAL_METERS` | number | 3 | Target distance interval for frame sampling |
| `BLUR_THRESHOLD_CONFIG` | number | 0.5 | Minimum threshold score for FFmpeg blurdetect filter acceptance |
| `PROCESSED_DATA_BUCKET` | string | `county-guardrail-processed-data-bucket` | S3 destination for extracted frames |

---

### Detection Service Adapter Layer & Model Integration

**Responsibility:** Abstract and handle communication between processing tasks and the underlying computer vision model (Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels), submitting usable frames and receiving bounding boxes and categories.
**Technology:** TypeScript module embedded within Fargate container tasks utilizing `@aws-sdk/client-rekognition`.

**Public Interface:**
```
submitFrameForDetection(frameBuffer: Buffer, modelArn: string): Promise<DetectionResult[]> — Submits frame buffer to Rekognition Custom Labels and parses response
parseBoundingBoxes(rekognitionResponse: DetectCustomLabelsCommandOutput): DetectionResult[] — Extracts normalized bounding boxes, categories, and confidence scores
filterDetectionsByConfidence(detections: DetectionResult[], threshold: number): DetectionResult[] — Filters raw detections against configured confidence threshold
```

**Dependencies:**
- Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels: Managed computer vision inference endpoint (`DetectCustomLS` / `DetectCustomLabels` API)

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Fargate frame processing task loads an extracted, quality-filtered still frame into memory.
2. Adapter layer wraps the image buffer and calls `DetectCustomLabels` against the active Rekognition model endpoint.
3. Adapter parses the JSON response, extracting bounding box coordinates, defect categories (broken/severed, bent/deformed, missing, corroded/rusted, misaligned/leaning posts), and confidence scores.
4. Adapter filters out detections falling below the versioned confidence threshold.
5. Filtered detection payloads are passed to the clustering and consolidation engine.

**Configuration:**
| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |

| `REKOGNITION_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD` | number | 80.0 | Minimum confidence percentage score required for valid detection |
| `MAX_RESULTS_PER_IMAGE` | number | 10 | Maximum bounding box detections allowed per frame |

### Detection Consolidation & Clustering Service

**Responsibility:** Cluster raw bounding-box detections of the same physical defect across multiple nearby frames using GPS proximity, time, and category into a single representative review item stored in DynamoDB.
**Technology:** Node.js / TypeScript service execution module running within AWS Fargate / Lambda processing tasks.

```

persistConsolidatedDefects(consolidatedItems: ConsolidatedDefectItem[]): Promise<void> — Writes deduplicated review items and metadata to Amazon DynamoDB
```

**Dependencies:**

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Collects all raw bounding-box detections generated across sequential processed frames for an inspection run.
2. Applies spatial clustering (GPS proximity within tolerance radius) and temporal/category matching to identify repeated hits of the same physical defect.
3. Collapses clustered detections into a single representative review item, selecting the frame with the highest confidence score for visual inspection overlay.
4. Writes consolidated defect items, bounding-box metadata, and initial queue status to Amazon DynamoDB.

**Responsibility:** Integrate confirmed damage findings and shared query logic with the county's existing Esri ArcGIS platform to support map dashboards, GIS layers, and export reporting.

```
generateInspectionReport(reportFormat: 'csv' | 'pdf', filterCriteria: ReportFilterCriteria): Promise<Buffer> — Compiles road/priority summaries and generates exportable report documents
```

**Dependencies:**

**Internal Logic Flow:**
1. Service receives scheduled or user-initiated requests for map data or inspection reports.
2. Service queries Amazon DynamoDB using shared query logic to retrieve confirmed damage records filtered by category, road segment, or priority.
3. For map dashboard requests, records are transformed into standard GeoJSON / Esri ArcGIS feature collection format.
4. For report requests, data is compiled into CSV exports or printable PDF inspection reports.
5. Payloads are returned to the caller or pushed to Esri ArcGIS REST endpoints.

| Config Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|

## 7. Integration Design

### County Active Directory (AD FS)

**Method:** REST API / SAML 2.0 / OIDC
**Direction:** Inbound
**Data Format:** JSON / SAML XML

**Auth Mechanism:**
- Type: OAuth 2.0 / SAML 2.0
- Credentials Storage: AWS Secrets Manager reference (`arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123456789012:secret:cc/adfs/saml-config`)

**Error Handling:**
- Retry Strategy: Exponential backoff, max 3 retries (via `@aws-sdk/client-cognito-identity-provider` built-in retry middleware)
- Circuit Breaker: Threshold: 5 failures in 60s, recovery: 30s (implemented via `opossum` circuit breaker library)
- Fallback: Reject user authentication request with HTTP 401 Unauthorized and redirect to login error screen
- Dead Letter Queue: N/A (Synchronous authentication flow; auth errors logged to Amazon CloudWatch Logs)

**Sequence:**
1. County Inspector initiates login from React Upload or Reviewer Application
2. Amazon Cognito redirects authentication request to County Active Directory via AD FS (SAML 2.0 / OIDC)
3. County AD FS validates user credentials and returns SAML assertion / tokens to Amazon Cognito
4. Amazon Cognito issues a secure JSON Web Token (JWT) back to the React Application
5. React Application includes the JWT bearer token in subsequent API requests; backend validates the token signature
6. On failure: AD FS returns authentication error; Amazon Cognito intercepts, logs the failure, and returns an HTTP 401 response to the React application

---

### Esri ArcGIS Platform

**Method:** REST API
**Direction:** Outbound
**Data Format:** JSON / GeoJSON

**Auth Mechanism:**
- Type: API Key / OAuth 2.0
- Credentials Storage: AWS Secrets Manager reference (`arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123456789012:secret:cc/esri/arcgis-credentials`)

**Error Handling:**
- Retry Strategy: Exponential backoff, max 3 retries (via `axios-retry` client configuration with 1000ms base delay)
- Circuit Breaker: Threshold: 5 failures in 60s, recovery: 30s (implemented via `opossum`)
- Fallback: Serve cached spatial data query results from Amazon DynamoDB / local memory cache and display a warning banner in the Esri ArcGIS map dashboard
- Dead Letter Queue: `processing-dlq` (Amazon SQS queue `arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:123456789012:cc-processing-dlq`) for failed batch GIS sync jobs

**Sequence:**
1. Esri ArcGIS Integration Service queries confirmed findings and shared query logic from Amazon DynamoDB
2. Esri ArcGIS Integration Service formats spatial data into GeoJSON payload
3. Esri ArcGIS Integration Service sends HTTP POST/PUT request to Esri ArcGIS REST API endpoint
4. Esri ArcGIS Platform validates spatial payload and updates map layers and dashboard views
5. Esri ArcGIS Platform responds with HTTP 200 OK and feature publication receipt
6. On failure: Integration Service catches error, increments retry count, triggers circuit breaker on persistent failure, and writes failed synchronization payload to `processing-dlq`

## 8. Security Design

### Authentication Implementation
- **Provider:** Amazon Cognito User Pools federated to county Active Directory via AD FS (Active Directory Federation Services)
- **Flow:** Authorization Code Flow with PKCE for the React Single Page Applications (Upload & Reviewer)
- **Token Format:** JSON Web Token (JWT) — claims: sub, email, custom:roles, exp, iss, aud
- **Token Lifetime:** access: 15min, refresh: 7days
- **Storage:** httpOnly secure cookie for refresh tokens, in-memory storage for access tokens in React application state

### Authorization Rules
| Endpoint | Admin | User | Guest | Notes |
|----------|-------|------|-------|-------|
| POST `/upload/presign` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Requires valid JWT with uploader or inspector role |
| GET `/defects` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Requires valid JWT with reviewer/inspector role |
| PATCH `/defects/{id}` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Requires valid JWT with reviewer/inspector role; logs audit trail |
| GET `/reports` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Requires valid JWT with inspector role |
| GET `/gis/query` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | Requires valid JWT |

### Input Validation
| Input | Validation Rules |
|-------|-----------------|
| Email | RFC 5322 format, max 255 chars, lowercase normalized |
| Video File Upload | MIME type `video/mp4` or `video/quicktime`, max file size 15GB, must contain valid GPMF telemetry header |
| Defect Status Update | Enum validation (`APPROVED`, `DISMISSED`, `RECATEGORIZED`), required review note if dismissed, valid target category enum if recategorized |
| Bounding Box Coordinates | Numeric float values between 0.0 and 1.0 representing normalized image dimensions |

### Data Sanitization
- **HTML:** DOMPurify — strip all tags except allowed list for review notes and textual report inputs
- **SQL:** Parameterized queries only — no string concatenation (enforced via Amazon DynamoDB DocumentClient / PartiQL parameter binding)
- **Path:** Reject `../` path traversal sequences, whitelist allowed alphanumeric and UUID characters for S3 object keys and file identifiers

### CORS Configuration
- **Allowed Origins:** `https://*.county-gov.internal`, `https://guardrail-ui.county-gov.internal`
- **Allowed Methods:** `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `OPTIONS`
- **Credentials:** `true`

### Rate Limiting
| Endpoint Group | Limit | Window | Key |
|---------------|-------|--------|-----|
| API Gateway Authentication & Upload Presign | 20 requests | per minute | User Principal (`sub` claim) / IP Address |
| Reviewer API (`/defects/*`) | 120 requests | per minute | User Principal (`sub` claim) |
| Report Generation (`/reports`) | 10 requests | per minute | User Principal (`sub` claim) |

### Audit Logging
| Event | Logged Fields | Level |
|-------|--------------|-------|
| User Login / Federation | user ID, IP address, success/fail, timestamp, AD FS assertion ID | info / warn |
| Video Upload Initiated | user ID, file name, file size, S3 key, timestamp | info |
| Defect Status Modified | reviewer ID, defect ID, action (approve/dismiss/recategorize), original label, corrected label, timestamp | info |
| Pipeline Execution Failure | task name, execution ARN, error code, error message, timestamp | error |

## 9. Error Handling & Logging Design

### Error Classification
| Category | HTTP Status | Error Code Pattern | Example |
|----------|------------|-------------------|---------|
| Validation | 400 | VALIDATION_* | VALIDATION_REQUIRED_FIELD |
| Authentication | 401 | AUTH_* | AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED |
| Authorization | 403 | AUTHZ_* | AUTHZ_INSUFFICIENT_ROLE |
| Not Found | 404 | NOT_FOUND_* | NOT_FOUND_USER |
| Business Logic | 422 | BIZ_* | BIZ_DUPLICATE_EMAIL |

```json
  "level": "INFO",
  "service": "service-name",
```

## 10. Design Traceability

### Requirement-to-Design Mapping
| Requirement | Design Component | Design Section | Status |
|------------|-----------------|---------------|--------|
| FR-001 | React Upload Application & Amazon Cognito / AD FS Integration | Section 2 (Authentication & Frontend) | Designed |
| FR-002 | AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction Service & GPMF Parser | Section 3 (Telemetry Extraction Service) | Designed |
| FR-003 | AWS Step Functions, MediaConvert, & AWS Fargate Frame Processing | Section 4 (Orchestration & Frame Extraction) | Designed |
| FR-004 | FFmpeg Blurdetect Filter Module | Section 4.3 (Frame Quality Filtering) | Designed |
| FR-005 | Detection Service Adapter & Rekognition Custom Labels API | Section 5 (AI Inference & Adapter Layer) | Designed |
| FR-006 | GPS Proximity & Time Clustering Engine | Section 6 (Detection Consolidation & Clustering) | Designed |
| FR-007 | React Reviewer Application & DynamoDB Audit Trail | Section 7 (Review Application & DynamoDB Schema) | Designed |
| FR-008 | Esri ArcGIS Integration Service & Reporting Exporter | Section 8 (Esri ArcGIS Integration & Reporting) | Designed |

### Architecture-to-Design Mapping
| Architecture Component | Design Implementation | Technology |
|-----------------------|----------------------|-----------|
| React Upload & Reviewer Applications | Single-page application bundle hosted via S3/CloudFront with secure API client | React 18, TypeScript, AWS SDK v3, ioredis (if caching), axios |
| Amazon Cognito & AD FS | OpenID Connect / SAML token exchange and JWT validation authorizer | Amazon Cognito User Pools, AWS API Gateway JWT Authorizer |
| Amazon S3 Raw Video Bucket | Direct presigned multipart upload endpoints and event notification routing | Amazon S3 SDK v3, @aws-sdk/s3-presigned-post |
| Amazon EventBridge | S3 object-created event rule mapping to Step Functions state machine ARN | AWS CDK (`aws-events-targets`), EventBridge Rule |
| AWS Step Functions Pipeline | State machine definition handling start/stop inference, Map state, and error handling | AWS Step Functions ASL (Amazon States Language) |
| AWS Elemental MediaConvert | Video segmentation and transcoding job configuration template | AWS SDK v3 MediaConvert Client |
| AWS Fargate Telemetry Extraction & Frame Processing | Containerized worker tasks executing GPMF parsing and FFmpeg processing | Node.js 20, fluent-ffmpeg, @gpmf-extract/node, Docker on ECS Fargate |
| Detection Service Adapter Layer | Adapter interface abstracting Rekognition Custom Labels API calls and error handling | TypeScript class wrapper over AWS SDK v3 Rekognition client |
| Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels | Computer vision object detection inference endpoint (`DetectCustomLabels`) | Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels API |
| Detection Consolidation & Clustering Service | Spatial-temporal clustering algorithm grouping bounding boxes by GPS haversine distance and timestamp | Turf.js (`@turf/distance`) in Node.js |
| Amazon DynamoDB | NoSQL tables for review queue items, audit logs, and training dataset references | DynamoDB DocumentClient (`@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb`) |
| Esri ArcGIS Integration Service | REST API integration and shared query logic generator for GeoJSON, CSV, and PDF outputs | Esri ArcGIS REST JS (`@arcgis/rest-request`), PDFKit |

### Open Design Questions
| # | Question | Impact | Assigned To |
|---|---------|--------|-------------|
| DQ-001 | What is the exact spatial distance tolerance (meters) and time window (seconds) for clustering raw detections of the same physical defect? | Impacts the deduplication accuracy and review queue size in FR-006 / Section 6. | Technical Lead / County Inspectors |
| DQ-002 | What is the specific FFmpeg `blurdetect` filter threshold value (e.g., epel/metric score) required to reject blurry GoPro frames without dropping valid damage? | Impacts frame quality filtering precision in FR-004 / Section 4.3. | Cloud/DevOps Lead / CV Engineer |
| DQ-003 | How should the Esri ArcGIS feature layer schema map directly to the DynamoDB consolidated defect item attributes? | Blocks finalization of Section 8 (Esri ArcGIS Integration). | County GIS Team / Integration Developer |

### Design Assumptions
| # | Assumption | Impact if Wrong |
|---|-----------|----------------|
| DA-001 | GoPro GPMF telemetry streams contain continuous, monotonically increasing timestamps and valid latitude/longitude coordinates without prolonged signal drops. | Telemetry extraction will fail or produce inaccurate GPS tracks, breaking the 3-meter distance sampling logic. |
| DA-002 | The Node.js `fluent-ffmpeg` wrapper and bundled FFmpeg binaries will execute successfully within the AWS Fargate container task resource limits (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM). | Frame extraction and blur filtering tasks may experience out-of-memory errors or slow processing speeds during high-resolution video decoding. |
| DA-003 | DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode will automatically handle read/write spikes during peak review operations without requiring manual capacity provisioning. | The React reviewer application could experience throttling or latency spikes during concurrent reviewer usage. |
